steps: Terminal velocity is the constant maximum velocity attained by a body falling through a fluid.
It is reached when the resistive force of the fluid balances the gravitational force, so the resultant force and acceleration become zero.
items.finalAnswer: Terminal velocity is the constant velocity attained by a falling body when the fluid’s resistive force balances its weight.

steps: He should fire the rocket in the direction opposite to the direction in which he wants to move.
The rocket gases move in one direction and, by Newton’s third law, exert an equal and opposite force on the astronaut, pushing him towards the spaceship.
items.finalAnswer: He should fire the rocket away from the spaceship.

steps: Given: Mass of the 60 kg skater, m₁ = 60 kg; mass of the 80 kg skater, m₂ = 80 kg; velocity gained by the 60 kg skater, v₁ = 4 m s⁻¹; initial momentum of the two skaters = 0.
Required: Velocity of the 80 kg skater and an explanation of Newton’s third law.
By Newton’s third law, the skaters exert equal and opposite forces on each other when they push off.
The forces act for the same time, so the impulses and changes in momentum are equal in magnitude and opposite in direction.
By conservation of momentum: m₁v₁ + m₂v₂ = 0.
Substitution: (60 kg)(4 m s⁻¹) + (80 kg)v₂ = 0.
Working: 240 kg m s⁻¹ + (80 kg)v₂ = 0; v₂ = −240/80 = −3 m s⁻¹.
The negative sign shows that the 80 kg skater moves in the direction opposite to the 60 kg skater.
items.finalAnswer: The 80 kg skater moves at 3 m s⁻¹ in the opposite direction; their momenta are equal and opposite.

steps: When a moving person is brought to rest, the change in momentum is the same whether an airbag or a seatbelt stops the person.
An airbag increases the time over which this change in momentum occurs.
Since force is the rate of change of momentum, increasing the stopping time reduces the force on the person and lowers the chance of injury.
items.finalAnswer: An airbag increases the time taken to stop the person, reducing the force produced by the change in momentum.

steps: The horse’s reasoning is wrong because the action and reaction forces act on different bodies; they do not cancel each other on one body.
The horse pulls the cart forward, while the cart pulls the horse backward with an equal force.
At the same time, the horse pushes the ground backward, and the ground exerts a forward frictional force on the horse.
This forward force from the ground can move the horse and cart forward if it is greater than the opposing forces.
items.finalAnswer: The action and reaction forces act on different bodies; the ground’s forward frictional force can accelerate the horse and cart.

steps: The fielder moves his or her hands backward while catching the ball to increase the time taken to bring it to rest.
The change in momentum of the ball is the same, but the rate of change of momentum is reduced when the stopping time is increased.
Therefore, the force exerted on the hands is reduced and the chance of injury is lessened.
items.finalAnswer: Drawing the hands backward increases the stopping time and reduces the force on the fielder’s hands.

steps: When the jumper pushes off the boat towards the bank, the boat is pushed in the opposite direction by an equal and opposite force.
The boat moves backward, away from the bank.
As a result, the jumper may lose the support of the boat before reaching the bank and fall into the water.
items.finalAnswer: The boat moves backward as the jumper pushes off, so the jumper may lose support and fall into the water.

steps: Without friction, a person could not walk because the feet would slip on the ground.
Vehicles could not move properly, turn, or stop by applying their brakes.
It would be difficult to hold objects, write with a pencil, or grip things.
Objects and machines would keep sliding, and many everyday activities that depend on grip would become impossible.
items.finalAnswer: Without friction, walking, gripping, writing, and controlling or stopping vehicles would become difficult or impossible.
